title: AI and Cloud Infrastructure Foundations
summary: Connect cloud services and AI workloads to the physical infrastructure that supports them.
objectives: Explain that cloud services depend on physical data-center systems.
Identify infrastructure resources a workload may require.

vocab.def: A set of computing tasks and resource demands.
The physical and software systems that support computing services.
Specialized hardware designed to perform certain computations efficiently.

sections.heading: Cloud still uses infrastructure
sections.body: A conceptual chain is user or application -> cloud service -> network -> compute -> storage -> physical data-center infrastructure. Cloud location and ownership may differ, but infrastructure does not disappear.

sections.heading: Infrastructure focus
sections.body: This specialization studies compute, storage, networking, power, cooling, reliability, and monitoring for AI and cloud workloads. It does not teach model development or vendor certification.

practice.prompt: What remains part of the system when an application uses a cloud service?
practice.answer: Physical compute, storage, networking, power, cooling, and operations still support the service.

quiz.question: What does cloud computing rely on?

lab.objective: Map a synthetic cloud service to supporting infrastructure.

futureCompetencyCandidates: map an infrastructure workload to supporting resources
reflectionPrompt: Which physical dependency is easiest to overlook in a cloud diagram?
